fields.title: Where Requests Go
fields.keyTakeaway: The fate of sent data is determined by contract rather than defaults, and minimizing what you send is more reliable than any terms.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: A user asks an assistant about their orders. Where does this text end up?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: This is the first question from an enterprise client and one of the first from a regulator. The answer must be known precisely rather than approximately, and must be reflected in documents.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: By sending a request to a provider, you transfer data to a third party. What happens to it is determined by contract, not defaults.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **[[training-on-customer-data|Training on customer data]].** The provider uses requests to improve models. Often enabled by default for consumer tiers, usually not for enterprise. Verified in terms, not assumed.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Storage for security.** The provider stores requests for some time to monitor abuse. Usually 30 days. Even with training disabled.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **[[zero-data-retention|Zero data retention]].** Requests are not saved at all. Not available to everyone and not always, usually by contract.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: *[[dpa|DPA]]* with the provider, defining roles and responsibilities. *Provider on the [[subprocessor|subprocessor]] list* and notifying users. *Geography awareness.* Where data is physically processed — a residency question from `DS3-N3`.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: A separate product decision — **what to send at all.** Minimization works better here than any contracts: data that wasn't sent cannot leak.
fields.sections/2/blocks/8/text: Practical techniques: do not send identifiers if the task doesn't require them; mask phones and addresses; send aggregates instead of raw records.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: What is sent to the model and what is not:
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/rows/4/1: No, only a disposable session identifier
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: The minimization rule had an unexpected side effect: the context became 40% shorter, meaning cheaper and faster.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Contract: training disabled, zero data retention mode, processing in the agreed region. Provider listed in subprocessor list, notification in privacy policy.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: The question from Domashniy retail chain — whether their buyers' data is leaked — was closed by this set of measures: training off, no storage, agreed region. A separate installation was not needed for this.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Provider terms change, and the mode effective at signing may change. It's worth checking upon renewal and tariff changes.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: The fate of sent data is determined by contract rather than defaults, and minimizing what you send is more reliable than any terms.
